title: Nonconvex Low-Rank Tensor Representation with Deep Priors for Multiview Subspace Clustering
claim: A multi-stage framework turns multi-view features into tensor self-representations, regularizes them with a deep prior and nonconvex low-rank terms, and then clusters.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right, three bracketed stages, with a feedback loop above
description: A wide, single-panel flow diagram on a light blue dashed background. On the left, flower photos pass through a Feature Extraction box and become per-view feature matrices X(1) to X(M). These are colored green and orange, and a self-expression equation X = XZ + E follows them. Per-view coefficient matrices Z(1) to Z(M) are stacked into a 3D tensor Z. The tensor is rotated and processed with t-SVD, shown in a green dashed box with a 'capped by τ' annotation. A yellow dashed box holds a neural-network deep prior and connects to the tensor Z in both directions. Below, the error matrices E(1) to E(M) are concatenated vertically and regularized by an l1/l2,1 norm 'capped by θ'. An information-fusion arrow along the top leads to an affinity matrix heatmap, then to clustering result groups of flowers. Curly braces below label the three stages: Multi-view Data, Self-representation Subspace Learning, and Clustering.

abstract: Multiview subspace clustering (MvSC) has shown remarkable potential in exploring underlying structures of high-dimensional data. However, existing MvSC methods still suffer from two shortcomings: (1) the commonly use of convex low-rank approximations inadequately capture high-order correlations across views, while sensitivity to noise and outliers degrades clustering performance, and (2) they lack the ability to preserve global correlations and local geometric patterns simultaneously. To address these issues, we propose a novel nonconvex regularized MvSC model with deep prior, which not only accurately characterizes the intrinsic low-rank structure and suppresses the effect of outliers, but also preserves local structural properties through deep networks. By mathematically analyzing the optimal solution of the optimization problem in our proposed model, we develop an efficient ADMM-based algorithm with provable convergence guarantees to solve it. Extensive experiments on various datasets demonstrate the superiority of the proposed model.
